title: He Sold The Eiffel Tower… Twice!

lines.text: In 1925, a charming master con artist named Mr. Victor Lustig sold the Eiffel Tower for scrap metal.
And then... he sold it a second time.
Back then, the Eiffel Tower was rusting, peeling, and costing Paris a fortune just to maintain.
Newspapers wrote that it might be torn down. So Mr. Lustig forged official French government credentials,
rented a luxury suite at the Hôtel de Crillon, and secretly summoned Paris's top scrap-metal dealers.
He claimed the demolition was a state secret to prevent public rioting—and opened bids for 7,000 tons of iron.
One wealthy dealer, Mr. André Poisson, desperately wanted the prestige—until he started getting suspicious.
Seeing him hesitate, Mr. Lustig played his masterstroke: he leaned in and quietly demanded a massive bribe.
That sealed the deal. Mr. Poisson thought: 'A corrupt bureaucrat taking a bribe? This must be the real government!'
Mr. Poisson handed over a fortune in cash, and Mr. Lustig caught the first train to Vienna with a suitcase full of francs.
Now here’s the insane part: Mr. Poisson was so paralyzed by shame, terrified of becoming the laughingstock of France,
that he never uttered a single word to the police!
When Mr. Lustig saw zero headlines in the papers, he realized he got away scot-free.
So he marched right back into Paris, booked another luxury suite, and sold the Eiffel Tower all over again to another victim!
Because in the end, Mr. Lustig wasn't selling an iron tower... he was selling human greed.
